title: I Think You Lost Your Mind
vol: Mommy Is Human Too · Book Ten
verse: Tell the truth, and tell it kindly. A home where truth is safe is a home where everyone can grow.

pages.text: I Think You Lost Your Mind

The day was running sideways and the list was running long,
and everything that Mommy touched seemed somehow to go wrong.

She put the milk into the pantry and the cereal on ice,
and looked for keys she held in hand — not once, not twice, but thrice!

She talked out loud to no one there; she stirred her tea with a pen;
she called the puppy "Jojo" — then called Jojo "Biscuit" again!

Then Pip stood in the doorway with her hands upon her hips:
"Mommy — I think you lost your mind!" came tumbling from her lips.

The kitchen went so quiet. Jojo froze. Bee dropped her spoon.
And Biscuit tiptoed out the room like he'd be leaving soon.

And Mommy almost snapped right back, "Don't talk to me that way!"
But then she stopped, and looked at Pip, and thought of what to say.

Because her girl had seen her clearly — frazzled, rushed, and spun —
and felt safe enough to tell her so. And that's a brave thing done.

So Mommy laughed a great big laugh and held up both the keys:
"You're right! My mind went on a trip. Somebody find it, please!"

Then Mommy knelt and pulled Pip close. "I'm glad that you can see,
and glad that you can tell me true. I want that, you and me.

But honest words can still be kind; they land much softer, too.
Next time try, 'Mommy, are you okay? You're acting not like you.'"

So Pip said, "Mommy, are you okay?" And Mommy said, "Not quite.
I'm tired, Pip. I'm doing a lot. I need some help tonight."

So Jojo put the milk away, and Pip found Mommy's shoes,
and Baby Bee brought her a hug — the best one she could choose.

Because a home where truth is safe, where hard words come out kind,
is where a child can always tell what's really on her mind.

Because your Mommy rushes, and gets frazzled through and through —
and Mommy loses her mind sometimes… because she's human too.

items: Is it okay to tell Mom when something seems wrong? How can you say it kindly?
How do you feel when someone tells you the truth?
What makes it safe to talk in our home?
Practice a kind way to say a hard thing.
Have a family talk night where everyone gets a turn.
